minimal_integration.preflight_environment: Noninteractive stdout pipes; PAGER=cat and MANPAGER=cat. Each command has at most 5 seconds, subject to the shared budget. No sudo or installation.

trigger_limits: Only existing output is observed. Producer test elapsed time and observer UTC/monotonic receipt time are both retained. Buffering or delayed scheduling can make the event stale; absent log progress is not proof that the UI remains stuck. Mark such a capture ambiguous, never assert exact boundary timing without supporting timestamps.

target_identity.preparation: Once the target method has launched its app, resolve its installed container on the exact selected simulator. Read its actual Info.plist with Python plistlib; verify CFBundleIdentifier and derive CFBundleExecutable. Resolve real paths and require the executable to be within that simulator's recorded dataPath/app container. Do not hard-code a guessed executable path.
target_identity.candidate_rule: Require exactly one live candidate whose complete comm path equals the derived executable path, whose UID equals the runner's UID and whose generation agrees with the method/launch event. An incomplete/truncated inventory, basename-only match, absent/ambiguous PID or failed identity command means no app sample.
target_identity.confirmation: Require lsof executable-text path evidence matching the same installed executable as well as the ps path/UID/start tuple. Revalidate immediately before and after sampling; compare sample header PID/path with the receipt. Never choose by pgrep/name, newest PID, a historical failure PID, or a similar bundle name.
target_identity.automation: Prefer one UI-test runner only if its actual built Runner.app Info.plist and generated xctestrun identify the runner belonging to this test build, and the same selected-simulator container/path/UID/start checks succeed. Do not assume a runner bundle-ID suffix. If it cannot be proved, optionally sample the directly owned live xcodebuild child instead, explicitly labeled client-only. Never sample arbitrary testmanagerd/CoreSimulator/system daemons.
target_identity.race_limit: PID plus path/start checks are not an atomic process handle. If the app exits or identity changes during capture, mark it invalid/partial and do not retry or attribute the sample to the new process.

proposed_read_only_capture_commands.note: These are argv shapes for future review, not commands executed in this context. Each placeholder is a validated value passed as an argument, without shell interpolation.
proposed_read_only_capture_commands.host_handling: Use the existing host probe's 5-second command limit and elapsed/status metadata. Start stack capture before host probes; run the small host probes alongside it so vm_stat cannot delay the app sample. Keep original before/after vm_stat/sysctl/ps/df probes and logs unchanged.
proposed_read_only_capture_commands.stack_scope: Retain all sampled threads, symbols/image data and raw report. Work on a Swift actor need not occur on the main thread.

bounds_and_cleanup.pre_boundary: At most one container resolution per role after the first launch, 5 seconds each; at most two roles. No unbounded discovery or tool retry loop.
bounds_and_cleanup.per_incident: One 30-second monotonic budget from the scheduled capture instant, with the last 5 seconds reserved for cleanup. Identity checks share at most 10 seconds. Each sample requests 5 seconds at 10 ms and has at most 10 seconds for collection/report, clipped to the shared work deadline. At most two sample children run concurrently.
bounds_and_cleanup.maximum: One incident capture per affected method/job; at most two affected jobs in one future diagnostic run. No second sample window, new test, automatic rerun or wider test timeout. The observer is disarmed at the existing test step's end even if no trigger occurs.
bounds_and_cleanup.output: Retain at most 4 MiB per sample, 1 MiB for the one process inventory, 64 KiB per other command stream and 12 MiB aggregate new diagnostic data per job. Enforce byte limits during collection, mark truncation and preserve receipts. For the sample -file output, the future child launcher must impose a 4 MiB RLIMIT_FSIZE before exec; apply it only to the diagnostic child, never the app/test client. This is a proposed implementation requirement, not an already verified runner feature.
bounds_and_cleanup.cancellation: Every diagnostic subprocess starts in its own new session, as in boot_simulator.py. On its deadline, output limit, method completion, app identity change, SIGINT/SIGTERM or test-step exit, kill only those newly owned diagnostic process groups and reap direct children within the remaining cleanup reserve (at most 2 seconds per child). Record partial files and cleanup failures. Never kill the sampled app, test runner, xcodebuild or simulator as diagnostic cleanup.
bounds_and_cleanup.actual_time: Record absolute UTC, monotonic start/deadline/finish and elapsed duration separately. Host scheduling can delay timeout handling; the previous host records demonstrate this. Do not claim a guaranteed wall-clock bound or subtract an absolute finish offset as if it were command duration.

evidence_and_interpretation.retention: Create an exclusive per-run/attempt/job/method directory; never overwrite previous evidence. Retain raw outputs, ownership receipts, trigger log offsets/excerpt, command receipts, partial failures and an atomic manifest. Add the directory to the existing full evidence artifact. Keep original xcresult, original attachments, test logs, startup receipts and before/after host logs; do not substitute compact summaries.
manifest: source and app/test blob SHAs; separately identified harness SHA
exact selectors and started/passed/failed method accounting
runner OS/architecture, Xcode/runtime and selected simulator inventory/UDID
actual built binary identity and matching symbol/image identifiers when available
PID/UID/start/path/container identity before and after; automation role
producer event time, observer time, sample window and boundary ambiguity
exact argv, configured deadlines, actual elapsed, exit status, timeout/truncation and cleanup status
byte lengths and SHA-256 of every retained original or explicitly labeled truncated prefix
decisions: Repeated app-owned frames or a blocked main thread/actor during a verified pending boundary can direct a source investigation; inspect all threads and symbols before proposing a fix.
An idle app plus an automation-side wait and normal host command timing is evidence to investigate the UI automation path, not proof that the app is correct.
Delayed read-only host commands or sampler startup show contemporaneous host responsiveness problems; they do not by themselves establish the cause of the UI assertion.
If ownership fails, logs are stale, stacks are unavailable/unsymbolicated, or the app has already terminated, record the gap. Post-termination samples cannot answer the in-flight question.
evidence_and_interpretation.repeat_rule: If the current run passes these boundaries, do not run this diagnostic plan. If a future single instrumented execution captures a repeated failure, inspect those stacks before deciding any next action. If it passes or misses capture, preserve that result and limitation; no blind retry and no success claim for earlier failed required tests.
